tweets.creator: @heavypulp
tweets.text: How to prompt for emotion: describe physical attributes and not just the emotion by itself. Instead of "angry", you can do: "His teeth stay clenched the entire clip, the jaw locked hard... the mouth a trap that words have to escape through. His eyes are open: stretched to their absolute widest, the whites showing, never blinking once...". Grok Imagine responds well to this descriptive writing style.

tweets.creator: @heavypulp
tweets.text: How to keep an actor consistent across different takes: keep everything that isn't the emotion or performance the same. Example of voice prompt that we would re-use for this scene: "low gravel baritone, authentic Greek-British hybrid accent, Mediterranean vowels under clipped British consonants." All the variance goes into the performance.

tweets.text: Orca ( @orca_build ) is a trending agent orchestrator - Kilo's Agent Manager solves a similar problem, just from inside VS Code. Both use git worktrees to run agents in isolation. Orca is its own desktop app that works across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kilo, and other 3rd-party agent tools. Kilo's version runs directly inside VS Code, where you can run the same prompt across 4 worktrees with different models side by side, then review and merge without leaving the editor. Read the full comparison blog: blog.kilo.ai/p/orca-vs-kilo-…

articles.content: Orca vs. Kilo Agent Manager - by Brian Turcotte - Kilo Blog Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in Orca vs. Kilo Agent Manager Comparing Two Popular Ways to Run Parallel AI Agents Brian Turcotte Jul 22, 2026 5 Share Kilo’s Agent Manager is a built-in feature of Kilo’s VS Code Extension that allows you to run multiple coding agents in parallel without conflict - which means you can have multiple agents work on different tasks at the same time, or run the same task across multiple different AI models and compare their work. Then, you can merge any of the changes that you want to keep from different agents without merge conflicts.
